城市中的一棵树，不只是道路旁的一处绿色。夏日里，树冠为行人遮去烈日；雨水到来时，根系与土壤共同调节地表径流。人们在树下等待、交谈，也在一年又一年的花开叶落中记住一个地方。
一座城市若只计算树木的数量，便容易忽略它们与街道、居民和时间的联系。保护老树，需要理解生长的节律，也需要为未来的树留下空间。城市建设的耐心，常常体现在这些细小而持久的选择中。
作者为什么说“一棵树，不只是道路旁的一处绿色”？结合文本简要分析。

READING PASSAGE 1
THE VALUE OF URBAN TREES
Urban trees are often valued for the shade they provide, but their contribution extends well beyond summer comfort. Their leaves intercept rainfall, while roots help water enter the soil. In streets with heavy traffic, the position and shape of the canopy can influence how people experience both heat and noise.
A recent local survey followed three neighbourhoods over five years. Streets with mature trees recorded lower afternoon surface temperatures than nearby streets without trees. Residents also reported that shaded routes made walking to shops more attractive. The researchers emphasised that tree cover alone did not explain every difference: the width of streets, building materials and access to public transport also mattered.
Long-term planning is therefore essential. A newly planted tree needs time, suitable soil and regular care. Replacing one mature tree with several small saplings may increase the number of trees on a register, yet it does not immediately replace the shade that has been lost.

1. What do tree leaves intercept?
2. How long did the local survey last?
3. What must planners provide in addition to time and care?

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
questions.solution:
The chart compares the proportion of trips made by bicycle in three cities in 2010 and 2020.

Overall, cycling accounted for a larger share of travel in two cities, but their rates of growth were very different. City A went from the lowest share to the highest, while City C was the only city where the share fell.

In 2010, City B led at 30%, followed by City C at 25%. By contrast, fewer than one in five journeys in City A were made by bicycle. Over the next ten years, City A’s share doubled from 18% to 36%. City B recorded a much smaller rise, of just two percentage points, and ended the period four points behind City A.

City C moved in the opposite direction, dropping six percentage points to 19%. As a result, the gap between the cities with the largest and smallest shares widened from 12 percentage points in 2010 to 17 in 2020.

sections.title: Writing task 2
sections.instructions: You should spend about 40 minutes on this task. Write at least 250 words.

questions.prompt:
Some people believe that cities should invest more in public transport than in new roads.
To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
questions.solution:
When choosing between new roads and better public transport, cities should generally give priority to buses and trains. That priority should guide investment in crowded areas, although particular road projects may still deserve funding.

The strongest reason for investing in public transport is that a city centre has limited space. A bus in a dedicated lane can carry dozens of people without requiring a separate lane or parking space for each traveller. Where buses are frequent enough that passengers need not plan their day around a timetable, some drivers may choose to leave their cars at home. This is why spending on reliable service can do more for everyday travel than adding another lane at a junction that will still be crowded at rush hour.

Public transport can also give people without cars more access to jobs and services. Consider a hospital where many employees finish work late. If the last train leaves before their shift ends, a larger road offers little help to staff who cannot afford a car. An evening bus linking the hospital with several neighbourhoods would address that problem directly. The value comes from where and when the service runs, not simply from buying more vehicles.

Nevertheless, some journeys cannot readily be made by public transport. In a district where freight lorries currently pass through a narrow residential street, a short bypass might improve safety more than an extra bus route. Cities should fund such projects when the intended benefit is specific and supported by local evidence.

I therefore favour public transport as the main priority, with road investment reserved for problems that better transit would not solve.
questions.explanation: The model takes a qualified position, explains two reasons through distinct examples, and identifies when targeted road spending is justified. A well-supported opposing position is also valid.

questions.solution:
Madame, Monsieur,

Je vous écris au sujet du projet de jardin partagé que notre ville souhaite créer. Je soutiens cette idée, car elle pourrait améliorer la vie du quartier de plusieurs façons.

Tout d’abord, ce jardin offrirait aux habitants un lieu pour se rencontrer. Les personnes qui vivent seules pourraient participer à des activités communes et échanger leurs connaissances. Les enfants découvriraient aussi comment poussent les légumes, au lieu de les voir seulement au supermarché.

Ensuite, cultiver une petite parcelle permettrait de produire des aliments frais et de mieux comprendre les saisons. À mon avis, il faudrait réserver quelques espaces aux écoles et organiser des ateliers gratuits pour les débutants.

Il existe cependant une difficulté : pendant les vacances, certaines parcelles risquent de manquer d’eau. Pour résoudre ce problème, je propose un calendrier d’arrosage commun et un système de récupération de l’eau de pluie. Chaque participant pourrait choisir une semaine de responsabilité.

Enfin, une réunion mensuelle aiderait à répartir les tâches et à régler les désaccords. Je serais heureuse de participer à la préparation du projet.

Je vous remercie de votre attention.

Cordialement,
Camille Martin
